issues.legal_issue: An election of municipal councillors cannot be held after a change in municipal limits unless the reconstituted municipality has first been divided into new wards.
material_facts: The State issued a notification to include local areas within the municipality, which would alter its limits.
The election rules and delimitation rules assigned the task of dividing the municipality into wards to a Delimitation Board and required ward readjustment when municipal limits changed.
The appellants challenged the election on the ground that there had been no ward delimitation or preparation of fresh electoral rolls.
issues.conclusion: When municipal limits are altered by inclusion or exclusion of a local area, the municipality must be delimited into new wards before councillors are elected.
issues.legal_principle: Under sections 5(3) and 7 of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, read with the Election Rules, 1952 and rules 4 and 6 of the Delimitation of Wards of Municipalities Rules, 1972, altered municipal limits require delimitation into new wards before an election, so that the electorate is fairly represented and no part is disenfranchised. The Court approved the reasoning in Bhaichandbhai Maganlal Shah v. The State of Gujarat and Ors.

predicates.municipal_council_election: The proceeding concerns an election of councillors to a municipality.
predicates.municipal_boundary_altered: The municipality's limits have changed through inclusion or exclusion of a local area.

issues.definition: When a municipal election concerns a municipality whose limits have changed, new ward delimitation is required before the election.

issues.legal_issue: An election held on existing municipal wards remains valid when an order kept a proposed boundary change from taking effect during the election and a mandatory election deadline required the election to proceed.
material_facts: A court order kept the inclusion notification in abeyance during the election, so the proposed local areas remained outside the municipal limits at that time.
A later appellate stay order had the same practical effect and remained in force during the election.
An amended statutory proviso required the State Government to hold the municipal elections before a specified deadline.
The State held the election on the basis of the existing municipal limits and wards; the stay was lifted only after the election.
The appellants argued that lifting the stay invalidated the election.
issues.conclusion: The election held on the basis of the existing wards was valid, and lifting the stay after the election did not invalidate it; the elected councillors could serve their full term.
issues.legal_principle: The Court treated the stay orders as keeping the proposed inclusion notification in abeyance during the election. Because the local areas had not then become part of the municipality and the amended proviso to section 13(3) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911 made holding the election before the deadline obligatory, the State could hold the election on the existing limits. The later lifting of the stay did not invalidate that election.

rule.if: municipal_election_challenge and inclusion_notification_stayed_at_election and election_deadline_was_mandatory and election_used_existing_wards

predicates.municipal_election_challenge: The proceeding challenges the validity of an election of municipal councillors.
predicates.inclusion_notification_stayed_at_electio: A court order kept a notification proposing to include local areas from taking effect when the election was held.
predicates.election_deadline_was_mandatory: The government was required to hold the election by a deadline while the stay was in effect.
predicates.election_used_existing_wards: The government held the election using the municipality's existing limits and wards.

issues.definition: If a municipal election is challenged after it was held on existing wards while a proposed inclusion was stayed and a mandatory deadline required the election, the election remains valid even after the stay is lifted.

issues.legal_issue: Residents of local areas kept outside a municipality by a court stay, and consequently denied electoral participation, may be given interim representation after those areas are included in the municipality.
material_facts: The local areas were included in the municipality under a notification, but court stay orders kept the notification from taking effect during the election.
Inhabitants of those areas who were otherwise eligible to vote were deprived of the opportunity to vote and to stand for election as councillors, President, or Vice-President.
The existing councillors had already been elected and were serving their term when the Court considered relief.
issues.conclusion: The included local areas were to be formed into one or more wards and given representation, with the term of their councillors ending alongside that of the existing councillors; this was an interim arrangement limited to the current council's term.
issues.legal_principle: Under section 5(5) of the Punjab Municipal Act, 1911, inhabitants of an included local area that is a Sabha area are to receive representation in the prescribed manner. Because the stay orders had deprived otherwise eligible inhabitants of electoral participation, the Court directed interim representation for the included areas, limited to the term of the existing council.

predicates.municipal_representation_proceeding: The proceeding concerns representation of residents in a municipality.
predicates.included_area_residents_were_denied_elec: Residents of an area included in a municipality were prevented from voting or standing for election because a court stay kept the inclusion from taking effect during the election.
predicates.current_council_is_serving: A council elected from the municipality's existing wards is serving when the representation issue is decided.

issues.definition: When a stay prevented residents of an included area from electoral participation and an existing council is serving, the included area receives interim representation.
